summary: Kuwait admits GCC nationals freely and issues eVisas and visas on arrival to citizens of around 50 countries — including the US, UK, EU member states and much of East Asia — for tourist stays of up to three months; everyone else needs a sponsored visit visa arranged in advance.

travelInsurance.text: Insurance is not checked for tourist entry, but medical care is expensive for visitors — comprehensive travel insurance is strongly recommended.

onwardTicket.text: Travelers entering on an eVisa or visa on arrival should hold a confirmed onward or return ticket; airlines may check before boarding.

currencyLimits.text: Cash or negotiable instruments worth KWD 3,000 or more (or the foreign-currency equivalent) must be declared on arrival.

notes: Alcohol may not be brought into Kuwait in any quantity, including duty-free purchases made en route. The country is completely dry.
Narcotics, pork products and pornographic material are prohibited; medications containing controlled substances need a prescription.

payments.text: Cards and contactless payments are accepted almost everywhere in Kuwait City, from malls to taxis. Cash is rarely needed beyond small souq purchases and tips.

safety.text: Kuwait has low crime and is generally safe for visitors. Regional tensions can flare with little notice, and strict local laws on alcohol, drugs and public behavior apply — follow your government's travel advice.

source.name: U.S. Department of State — Kuwait Travel Advisory

bestTimeToVisit.text: November to March brings mild, pleasant weather for the Corniche, souqs and desert trips; summer is among the hottest on Earth, regularly exceeding 45°C.

tips.text: Kuwait is a fully dry country — alcohol is illegal to import, buy or consume anywhere, with penalties including fines, imprisonment and deportation.
Travelers whose passports show Israeli stamps or visas are routinely refused entry to Kuwait — travel on a clean passport if you have previously visited Israel.
From June to September temperatures regularly exceed 45°C. Plan outdoor activities for early morning or after dark and stay hydrated.
During Ramadan, eating, drinking or smoking in public during daylight hours is an offense for everyone, including visitors — hotels serve food discreetly.
Apply for the eVisa only through the Kuwait Ministry of Interior's official portal — third-party websites charge large markups for the same visa.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Kuwait?
faq.answer: GCC nationals enter freely without a visa. Citizens of around 50 countries — including the US, UK, EU member states, Canada, Australia, Japan and South Korea — can obtain a KWD 3 eVisa online or a visa on arrival at Kuwait International Airport. All other nationalities need a visit visa arranged in advance through a sponsor in Kuwait or a Kuwaiti embassy.

faq.question: How does Kuwait's visa on arrival work?
faq.answer: Eligible nationalities pay KWD 3 at Kuwait International Airport for a tourist visa on arrival, typically allowing a stay of up to three months. Applying online in advance through the official eVisa portal is faster and avoids lines at the visa counter.

faq.question: How much does the Kuwait eVisa cost?
faq.answer: The tourist eVisa costs KWD 3 (roughly USD 10). Apply only through the Ministry of Interior's official portal and confirm the exact fee during the application — third-party sites add heavy service charges.

faq.question: Can I enter Kuwait with an Israeli stamp in my passport?
faq.answer: No. Kuwait does not admit Israeli passport holders, and travelers of any nationality whose passports show Israeli stamps or visas are routinely refused entry. Use a clean passport if you have previously visited Israel.

faq.question: Can tourists drink alcohol in Kuwait?
faq.answer: No. Kuwait is completely dry — alcohol cannot legally be imported, sold or consumed anywhere in the country, including hotels, and penalties for violations are severe.
